meta.subject: history
meta.description: General world history facts: timelines, key events, important figures, cause-and-effect relationships, historical documents, historical thinking skills

facts.statement: BCE (Before Common Era) and BC (Before Christ) count backwards from year 1; CE (Common Era) and AD (Anno Domini) count forward from year 1
A decade is 10 years, a century is 100 years, and a millennium is 1,000 years
The Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age describe periods of human history based on the primary materials used for tools
The Agricultural Revolution (around 10,000 BCE) was when humans first began farming, leading to permanent settlements and the rise of civilizations
Major historical eras include Ancient (before 500 CE), Medieval (500-1500 CE), Early Modern (1500-1800), and Modern (1800-present)
The 21st century began on January 1, 2001; centuries are numbered one ahead of the hundreds digit (the 1900s are the 20th century)
Primary sources are firsthand accounts from the time period (diaries, letters, photos); secondary sources analyze events after the fact (textbooks, documentaries)
History is typically divided into prehistory (before written records) and history (after the invention of writing around 3500 BCE)
Humans (Homo sapiens) have existed for approximately 300,000 years, but written history covers only the last 5,500 years

common_errors.wrong: the year 2000 was in the 20th century
common_errors.correct: The year 2000 was the last year of the 20th century. The 21st century began on January 1, 2001.

common_errors.wrong: BCE dates get bigger as you move forward in time
common_errors.correct: BCE dates count backwards: 500 BCE is later than 1000 BCE. As BCE numbers get smaller, you are moving forward in time toward year 1.

common_errors.wrong: history only includes written records
common_errors.correct: Historians also use archaeology, oral traditions, artifacts, and scientific methods like carbon dating to understand the past before written records.

common_errors.wrong: AD stands for 'After Death' (of Jesus)
common_errors.correct: AD stands for Anno Domini, Latin for 'In the Year of Our Lord.' It counts from the estimated birth year of Jesus, not his death.

facts.statement: The invention of the printing press (c. 1440) led to increased literacy, the spread of new ideas, and contributed to both the Renaissance and the Reformation
The harsh terms of the Treaty of Versailles (1919) contributed to economic hardship and resentment in Germany, helping fuel the rise of Adolf Hitler and World War II
The Industrial Revolution caused mass urbanization, changed family structures, created new social classes, and led to both economic growth and labor exploitation
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in 1914 was the immediate trigger for World War I, though underlying causes included alliances, imperialism, and nationalism
The Black Death (1347-1351) killed roughly one-third of Europe's population, leading to labor shortages, higher wages for workers, and weakened feudalism
European colonization of the Americas caused the Columbian Exchange: new crops spread between continents, but European diseases devastated Indigenous populations
The Enlightenment's emphasis on reason, natural rights, and social contracts inspired both the American Revolution (1776) and the French Revolution (1789)
The development of agriculture around 10,000 BCE led to permanent settlements, surplus food, population growth, specialized labor, and eventually cities and civilizations
The fall of the Western Roman Empire (476 CE) led to political fragmentation in Europe, the rise of feudalism, and the beginning of the Middle Ages
The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945 led to Japan's surrender, the end of WWII, and the beginning of the nuclear age and Cold War arms race

common_errors.wrong: historical events have only one cause
common_errors.correct: Most major historical events have multiple causes. For example, WWI was caused by alliances, imperialism, nationalism, and militarism -- not just one assassination.

common_errors.wrong: historical events only have immediate effects
common_errors.correct: Events have both short-term and long-term effects. The fall of Rome had immediate political effects but also shaped European culture for centuries.

common_errors.wrong: correlation means causation in history
common_errors.correct: Just because two events happened at the same time does not mean one caused the other. Historians carefully analyze evidence to establish causal relationships.

common_errors.wrong: history always repeats itself exactly
common_errors.correct: While historical patterns can recur, circumstances are always different. It is more accurate to say that history can rhyme or echo, not repeat exactly.

facts.statement: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt; she was of Greek Macedonian descent, not ethnically Egyptian
Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement using nonviolent civil disobedience, inspiring civil rights movements worldwide
Confucius was a Chinese philosopher (551-479 BCE) whose teachings on ethics, family, and government shaped East Asian culture for over 2,000 years
Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences (physics and chemistry)
Harriet Tubman escaped slavery and helped approximately 70 other enslaved people reach freedom through the Underground Railroad
Simon Bolivar led independence movements across South America, freeing Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia from Spanish rule
Queen Elizabeth I of England (1533-1603) led England through a golden age of exploration and culture, including the defeat of the Spanish Armada
Frederick Douglass escaped slavery and became one of the most powerful voices for abolition and civil rights in 19th-century America
Eleanor Roosevelt championed human rights and helped draft the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) as chair of the UN Human Rights Commission
Nelson Mandela fought apartheid in South Africa, spent 27 years in prison, and became the country's first democratically elected Black president in 1994

common_errors.wrong: Cleopatra was Egyptian
common_errors.correct: Cleopatra was ethnically Greek, a member of the Macedonian Ptolemaic dynasty that ruled Egypt after Alexander the Great's conquest.

common_errors.wrong: Gandhi was the first president of India
common_errors.correct: Gandhi never held political office. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India, and Rajendra Prasad was the first President.

common_errors.wrong: Einstein failed math in school
common_errors.correct: Einstein excelled at mathematics. This myth may have started from a misunderstanding of Swiss grading scales.

common_errors.wrong: Columbus was the first person to reach the Americas
common_errors.correct: Indigenous peoples lived in the Americas for thousands of years. Norse explorer Leif Erikson reached North America around 1000 CE, nearly 500 years before Columbus.

common_errors.wrong: historical figures acted alone without help
common_errors.correct: Most famous historical achievements involved collaboration, support from communities, and contributions from many unnamed people. History often highlights individuals while overlooking groups.

facts.statement: The Magna Carta (1215) limited the power of England's king and established that the ruler must obey the law, influencing later democratic documents
The Declaration of Independence (1776) declared American independence and stated that all men are created equal with unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness
The U.S. Constitution (1787) is the oldest written national constitution still in use, establishing the framework of American government
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) was the first global document to list fundamental rights that all people are entitled to
The Code of Hammurabi (c. 1754 BCE) from Babylon is one of the oldest known written legal codes, establishing laws and punishments
The Enlightenment was an 18th-century intellectual movement emphasizing reason, individual rights, and the social contract between governments and the governed
The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (1789) was a key document of the French Revolution declaring that men are born free and equal in rights
The Emancipation Proclamation (1863) declared enslaved people in Confederate states to be free, transforming the Civil War into a fight to end slavery
The Geneva Conventions (1949) established international legal standards for humanitarian treatment during war, protecting civilians and prisoners of war
John Locke's ideas about natural rights (life, liberty, property) and government by consent directly influenced Thomas Jefferson's writing of the Declaration of Independence

common_errors.wrong: the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution are the same document
common_errors.correct: The Declaration (1776) announced independence from Britain. The Constitution (1787) established the framework of the US government. They are separate documents with different purposes.

common_errors.wrong: the Magna Carta created democracy
common_errors.correct: The Magna Carta limited the king's power and established rule of law, but it did not create democracy. It primarily benefited nobles, not common people.

common_errors.wrong: human rights have always been universally recognized
common_errors.correct: The concept of universal human rights developed over centuries. Slavery, serfdom, and denial of rights to women and minorities were considered normal for most of history.

common_errors.wrong: ancient laws were always unjust
common_errors.correct: While ancient legal codes had harsh punishments and reflected their societies' values, they also represented important steps toward organized justice and rule of law.

facts.statement: Primary sources are original materials from the time being studied: letters, diaries, photographs, artifacts, government records, and speeches
Secondary sources interpret and analyze primary sources: textbooks, biographies, documentaries, and scholarly articles written after the events
Historical bias means that all sources reflect the perspective, beliefs, and limitations of the person who created them
Context means understanding the time period, culture, and circumstances in which an event occurred, which helps explain why people acted as they did
Historians use multiple sources and cross-reference evidence to build a more complete and accurate picture of the past
Archaeology is the study of human history through physical remains like buildings, tools, pottery, and bones
Continuity and change is a key concept in history: some things stay the same over time while others transform dramatically
Historical empathy means trying to understand how people in the past thought and felt based on their circumstances, not judging them solely by modern standards
Carbon-14 dating is a scientific method that helps determine the age of organic materials up to about 50,000 years old
Oral history is the collection of memories and personal reflections through recorded interviews, valuable for understanding experiences not captured in written records

common_errors.wrong: primary sources are always more accurate than secondary sources
common_errors.correct: Primary sources can contain bias, errors, or incomplete information. A diary entry may be emotionally biased. Secondary sources can provide broader analysis and context.

common_errors.wrong: history is just a list of facts and dates to memorize
common_errors.correct: History involves analyzing evidence, understanding multiple perspectives, evaluating causes and effects, and constructing arguments supported by evidence.

common_errors.wrong: there is only one correct interpretation of history
common_errors.correct: Historians often disagree on interpretations because they may emphasize different evidence, perspectives, or analytical frameworks. New evidence can change understanding.

common_errors.wrong: older civilizations were less intelligent than modern people
common_errors.correct: People throughout history have been equally capable. Ancient peoples built pyramids, developed mathematics, created complex governments, and solved problems with the tools available to them.

facts.statement: The American Revolution (1775-1783) established the United States as an independent nation based on principles of self-governance and natural rights
The French Revolution (1789-1799) overthrew the monarchy and established ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity that influenced democratic movements worldwide
The Haitian Revolution (1791-1804) was the only successful large-scale slave revolt in history, establishing Haiti as the first free Black republic
The women's suffrage movement fought for decades to win women the right to vote; New Zealand was the first country to grant it in 1893, and the US followed in 1920
The abolitionist movement fought to end slavery; it succeeded in Britain's colonies in 1833 and in the United States with the 13th Amendment in 1865
The Industrial Revolution (beginning around 1760 in Britain) transformed economies from agricultural to manufacturing, changing how people lived and worked
Latin American independence movements in the early 1800s, led by figures like Simon Bolivar and Jose de San Martin, freed most of South America from Spanish rule
The Chinese Communist Revolution (1949) established the People's Republic of China under Mao Zedong, transforming the most populous country in the world
The anti-apartheid movement in South Africa fought against racial segregation and discrimination, ultimately leading to free elections in 1994
The Scientific Revolution (16th-17th centuries) transformed understanding of the natural world through observation and experimentation, led by figures like Galileo, Newton, and Copernicus

common_errors.wrong: revolutions always lead to immediate improvement
common_errors.correct: Revolutions often lead to periods of instability, violence, and uncertainty before positive change is achieved. The French Revolution led to the Reign of Terror before stability returned.

common_errors.wrong: social change happens suddenly
common_errors.correct: Most social movements build over decades of organizing, protest, and advocacy before achieving major change. The women's suffrage movement took over 70 years.

common_errors.wrong: only violent revolutions create change
common_errors.correct: Many successful movements used nonviolent methods. Gandhi's independence movement, the US Civil Rights Movement, and the anti-apartheid movement all achieved change through nonviolent resistance.

common_errors.wrong: revolutions are led by a single person
common_errors.correct: While history often highlights individual leaders, revolutions involve mass participation by thousands of ordinary people whose contributions are often unrecorded.

facts.statement: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes connecting China, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe from about 130 BCE to 1453 CE
Trade along the Silk Road spread not only goods (silk, spices, gold) but also ideas, religions (Buddhism, Islam, Christianity), and technologies (paper, gunpowder, compass)
The Columbian Exchange (after 1492) transferred crops, animals, and diseases between the Old World and the New World, permanently changing diets and populations on both sides
The transatlantic slave trade (16th-19th centuries) forcibly transported an estimated 12.5 million Africans to the Americas, profoundly shaping the economies and cultures of both continents
The Indian Ocean trade network connected East Africa, the Middle East, India, and Southeast Asia for over 2,000 years, exchanging spices, textiles, and precious metals
The spread of major world religions (Buddhism, Christianity, Islam) followed trade routes, carried by merchants, missionaries, and travelers
Paper was invented in China around 105 CE, spread to the Islamic world by the 8th century, and reached Europe by the 12th century, revolutionizing record-keeping
Crops like potatoes, tomatoes, and corn (maize) originated in the Americas and became staple foods in Europe, Africa, and Asia after the Columbian Exchange

common_errors.wrong: the Silk Road was a single road
common_errors.correct: The Silk Road was a vast network of many interconnected trade routes spanning thousands of miles across land and sea.

common_errors.wrong: trade only involved luxury goods
common_errors.correct: While luxury items like silk and spices were traded, everyday goods, agricultural products, and raw materials were also exchanged, along with ideas, religions, and technologies.

common_errors.wrong: cultural exchange only happened through trade
common_errors.correct: Culture also spread through conquest, migration, diplomacy, religious missions, and intermarriage. Trade was one important mechanism among many.

common_errors.wrong: tomatoes and potatoes have always been eaten in Europe
common_errors.correct: Tomatoes and potatoes are native to the Americas. They reached Europe only after Columbus's voyages in 1492 and took decades to be widely accepted as food.

facts.statement: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam are the three major Abrahamic religions, all tracing their origins to the patriarch Abraham and originating in the Middle East
Hinduism is one of the world's oldest religions, originating in the Indian subcontinent over 4,000 years ago, with no single founder
Buddhism was founded by Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) in India around the 5th century BCE and spread throughout Asia along trade routes
Islam was founded by the Prophet Muhammad in the 7th century CE in Arabia and spread rapidly across the Middle East, North Africa, and beyond
Christianity originated in the 1st century CE in the Roman province of Judea and grew from a small sect to the official religion of the Roman Empire by 380 CE
Monotheism is the belief in one God (Judaism, Christianity, Islam); polytheism is the belief in many gods (ancient Greek, Roman, Hindu traditions)
The Crusades (1096-1291) were a series of religious wars between European Christians and Muslims for control of the Holy Land
Religious tolerance has varied throughout history; some periods and empires (Persian, Mughal under Akbar) practiced tolerance, while others persecuted religious minorities

common_errors.wrong: all religions worship the same way
common_errors.correct: Religions have vastly different practices, beliefs, sacred texts, and forms of worship. Even within a single religion, denominations can differ significantly.

common_errors.wrong: religion and science have always been in conflict
common_errors.correct: Many scientists throughout history have been deeply religious. Islamic scholars preserved and advanced Greek science, and medieval monasteries were centers of learning.

common_errors.wrong: Hinduism has only one god
common_errors.correct: Hinduism is complex -- some traditions are polytheistic (many gods), some are monotheistic (one supreme being with many forms), and some are philosophical rather than theistic.

common_errors.wrong: the Crusades were purely about religion
common_errors.correct: The Crusades also involved political power, territorial ambition, economic motives (trade routes), and social factors alongside religious motivations.

facts.statement: The invention of writing (c. 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia) is one of the most important developments in human history, enabling record-keeping, laws, and the transmission of knowledge
Gunpowder, invented in China around the 9th century CE, transformed warfare when it spread to Europe and the Middle East
The magnetic compass, invented in China during the Han Dynasty, revolutionized navigation and made long-distance sea travel possible
The printing press (c. 1440) by Gutenberg made books affordable and widespread, dramatically increasing literacy and the spread of ideas
The telegraph, patented by Samuel Morse in 1837, was the first technology to allow near-instant communication over long distances
The discovery of penicillin by Alexander Fleming in 1928 revolutionized medicine and saved millions of lives by treating bacterial infections
The development of the internet in the late 20th century transformed communication, commerce, and access to information worldwide
The Green Revolution of the mid-20th century introduced high-yield crop varieties and modern farming techniques, dramatically increasing food production worldwide

common_errors.wrong: ancient people had no technology
common_errors.correct: Ancient civilizations developed sophisticated technologies including irrigation systems, bronze and iron working, road networks, aqueducts, and architectural techniques like the arch and dome.

common_errors.wrong: all important inventions came from Europe
common_errors.correct: Many key inventions originated in China (paper, gunpowder, compass, printing), the Islamic world (algebra, optics), India (decimal system, zero), and other regions.

common_errors.wrong: technology always improves people's lives
common_errors.correct: While technology has many benefits, it can also have negative effects like environmental damage, job displacement, warfare, and privacy concerns.

common_errors.wrong: inventions are always created by a single genius
common_errors.correct: Most inventions build on the work of many people over time. The light bulb, telephone, and computer all had multiple contributors before becoming practical.
